_doc: Calibration examples injected into the chat system prompt. Each example pairs a user prompt with the ideal first-call decision: a tool to invoke, the args, and a confidence score [0.0-1.0]. Confidence < 0.6 means DO NOT call the tool — call ASK_USER instead. The list is intentionally short — every example here ships on every chat turn.

examples.prompt: buy 10 RELIANCE at market
examples.note: Single deterministic action, all required fields present. NEVER use propose_workflow for one-shot orders.

examples.prompt: create a SIP of 5000 in NIFTYBEES on the 5th of every month
examples.note: SIP is an automation, not an agent. ALWAYS use create_sip for recurring fixed-amount investments.

examples.prompt: every Monday at 9:15 buy 10 NIFTYBEES at market
examples.note: Recurring schedule + single instrument + fixed qty + NO second action → propose_scheduled_order. NOT propose_workflow.

examples.prompt: every Monday 09:15 buy 5 NIFTYBEES and at Monday close sell my entire NIFTYBEES holding if RSI(14) is below 30

args._steps_summary: trigger.market_relative_time(open Mon) → action.place_order(buy 5) → trigger.market_relative_time(close Mon) → fetch.indicator(rsi 14) → condition.numeric → fetch.portfolio → action.place_order(sell)

examples.note: TWO triggers / TWO branches → propose_workflow, NEVER propose_scheduled_order. Whenever the prompt has 'AND … at <other time>' or any conditional second leg, route to propose_workflow.

examples.prompt: buy 50 TCS at market when its price drops below 3500
examples.note: Single-symbol price threshold, no expiry → propose_threshold_order. ABSOLUTE price level required (not 'X% below open').

examples.prompt: sell my entire INFY holding when it crosses 1700
examples.note: Acts on existing holding → propose_holding_action. Quantity comes from holding lookup at fire time.

examples.prompt: invest 100000 equally across the top 5 steel stocks every Monday at 9:20
examples.note: Sector basket — propose_basket_allocation hydrates the screener + allocate steps. Steel is a canonical sector.

examples.prompt: buy some Tata at market

args.question: Several Tata stocks are listed — TATAMOTORS, TATASTEEL, TATAPOWER, TCS, TATACONSUM. Which one, and how many shares?

examples.note: Ambiguous symbol AND missing quantity. Two missing fields → one focused question covering both.

examples.prompt: buy 50000 of HDFCBANK

args.question: Did you mean 50,000 shares of HDFCBANK or ₹50,000 worth (≈30 shares at current price)?

examples.note: Unit ambiguity (rupees vs shares) — never assume.

examples.prompt: what's the price of reliance
examples.note: Single-symbol price lookup. NEVER use propose_workflow for a quote.

examples.prompt: show me my holdings
examples.note: Read-only portfolio query. No agent.

examples.prompt: make it 25 instead of 30

args._steps_summary: Re-emit the prior threshold draft with threshold:25 (was 30). Carry over symbol, side, quantity, kind, schedule from the prior turn UNCHANGED. Do NOT ASK for size/qty/symbol again — they were already set.

examples.note: When the immediately-preceding turn drafted a *_threshold_* / *_scheduled_* / propose_workflow, and the user replies with a NUMBER tweak ('make it 25', 'lower to 20', 'change to 5%') — re-emit the SAME tool with only the changed number. NEVER re-ask for parameters the prior turn already established. NEVER route to a different propose_* tool.

examples.prompt: lower ADX to 20

args._steps_summary: Re-emit the prior workflow with the ADX condition value changed from 25 → 20. Carry over ALL other steps unchanged. Output is the FULL updated steps[], not a diff.

examples.note: Tweaking an indicator threshold inside a workflow draft: stay in propose_workflow. NEVER route to propose_scheduled_order, create_sl_order, or any other tool when editing a workflow's internal numbers.

examples.prompt: try it with 20/50 SMA instead

args._steps_summary: Re-run backtest_workflow with SMA periods updated to 20/50 (was 10/20). Carry over symbol, period (e.g. 3y), entry/exit shape. Emit the full steps[] with the new periods.

examples.note: Backtest parameter tweaks ('try with 20/50', 'use 14-period RSI instead', 'over 5 years instead'): re-emit backtest_workflow with the changed numbers. NEVER switch to get_multiple_indicators or get_indicator. The prior backtest draft is in scope — change only what the user named.

examples.prompt: cancel that

args.question: Cancelling the pending draft. Confirm — say 'yes' and I'll discard it.

examples.note: When the IMMEDIATELY-PRECEDING assistant turn proposed a draft (order, workflow, basket, SIP) and the user replies 'cancel', 'cancel that', 'never mind', 'drop it', or 'no don't' — DO NOT create a new order or call any propose_* tool. The runtime cancels the active draft. If unsure, route to ASK_USER asking for confirmation. NEVER interpret 'cancel that' as a fresh order.

examples.prompt: make it 50/100 SMA instead, and add an 8% profit target

args._steps_summary: Edit the active draft in-place: change indicator periods to 50/100, append a sell trigger when unrealized P&L >= 8%. Emit the FULL updated draft, not just the diff.

examples.note: Workflow modifications (changing thresholds, adding profit targets / stop-losses, swapping indicator periods, adding notify steps) STAY in propose_workflow. NEVER route to create_sip, place_market_order, or another macro when extending an existing draft. Emit the full updated steps[].

examples.prompt: backtest buy when RSI < 30 on RELIANCE over the last 5 years
examples.note: Single-indicator backtest. ALWAYS call backtest_workflow with the full steps[] shape. NEVER call run_backtest — legacy path.

examples.prompt: Backtest: every weekday morning, buy 1 INFY share if its debt-to-equity ratio is below 0.5. Use the last 2 years.
examples.note: Fundamentals-gated backtest. The user explicitly said 'Backtest:' AND named a fundamental gate → ALWAYS route to backtest_workflow (run it) and ALWAYS emit fetch.fundamental + condition.numeric. NEVER drop the fundamental gate. Named metrics include: roe, roce, roa, debt_to_equity, current_ratio, quick_ratio, eps_basic, revenue, net_profit, net_profit_margin, ebitda_margin, price_to_book, ev_to_ebitda, earnings_yield, interest_coverage, book_value_per_share, asset_turnover. Legacy short codes pe/roe/de/mcap still accepted.

examples.prompt: Backtest the last 3 years: every Monday buy 1 RELIANCE if its ROCE is above 10 percent.
examples.note: ROCE, current_ratio, ebitda_margin, eps_basic, and every other named field in financials_db.FIELD_MAP work the same way — emit metric: '<name>' literally. Do NOT default to legacy short codes pe/roe/de when a longer named field fits better.

examples.prompt: Backtest 3 years: buy 1 RELIANCE every Monday if ROIC is above 8 percent. Compute ROIC as (net_profit + interest_expense) / (total_equity + total_debt) * 100 if not built-in.
examples.note: When the user asks for a derived metric that isn't in FIELD_MAP (ROIC, FCF margin, custom score, etc.), emit metric: 'formula' with a formula string built ONLY from named FIELD_MAP identifiers and arithmetic (+ - * / ** %, parentheses, numeric literals). NO function calls, NO attribute access. Use formulas ONLY when no named metric fits — never wrap a named metric in a redundant formula.

examples.prompt: pharma stocks with P/E under 25
examples.note: Cross-sectional fundamental screens ARE supported via screen_fundamentals (fields: pe, roe, roce, de, payout; optional coarse sector pharma/bank/it/energy/auto/metal/finance/chemicals/fmcg/infra/textiles). Call it DIRECTLY for 'X stocks with ROE>N', 'cheap banking stocks', 'low debt high roe' — do NOT deflect to a fixed ticker list. Data is basic and may include small-caps; never invent names or numbers.

examples.prompt: Buy 5 RELIANCE at open. At 10 AM IST, if RBI announces a repo rate cut, sell my entire RELIANCE holding; otherwise hold for the day.

args._steps_summary: trigger.schedule(cron: 0 9 * * 1-5, market-open) → action.place_order(buy 5 RELIANCE market) → trigger.schedule(cron: 0 10 * * 1-5, 10 AM IST) → fetch.news(keywords: ["RBI","repo rate","MPC","rate cut"], event_description: "RBI announces a repo rate cut", min_confidence: 0.85) → condition.boolean(left: {{context.3.matched}}, value: true) → action.place_order(sell entire RELIANCE holding) ; on false branch: notify.message(hold for the day)

examples.note: News-gated intraday workflow. Use propose_workflow whenever a workflow has a news condition gating a downstream order. fetch.news's `matched` aggregate feeds condition.boolean.

examples.prompt: create me an agent that buys the top gainers after the open and sells them before the close.

args._steps_summary: trigger.market_relative_time(anchor: open, offset_minutes: 15) → fetch.top_movers(direction: gainers, universe: nifty50, limit: 5) → action.allocate_notional(symbols: {{context.1.symbols}}, side: buy, total_inr: 25000, strategy: equal) → trigger.market_relative_time(anchor: close, offset_minutes: -10) → action.squareoff(scope: all)

examples.note: Dynamic top-movers basket — NOT a single arbitrary stock. "top gainers/losers" is served by fetch.top_movers (Kite-primary NIFTY-50 movers) feeding action.allocate_notional which spreads a rupee budget equally across the movers via the {{context.<fetch_idx>.symbols}} ref. "buy at open, sell before close" is a two-leg intraday shape: trigger.market_relative_time(open) enters, a second trigger.market_relative_time(close) + action.squareoff(scope: all) exits. Never collapse a top-gainers ask into one ticker.

examples.prompt: If SEBI penalises any large private bank by 3 PM, short that bank's holding; otherwise hold.

args._steps_summary: trigger.schedule(cron: 0 15 * * 1-5) → fetch.news(keywords: ["SEBI","penalty","private bank","fine"], event_description: "SEBI imposes a penalty on a large private bank", min_confidence: 0.85) → condition.boolean(left: {{context.1.matched}}, value: true) → action.place_order(short the named bank from top_article) ; on false branch: notify.message(no SEBI action, holding)

examples.note: Time-bounded news check inside a scheduled workflow. fetch.news's top_article carries the named entity downstream actions can interpolate via {{context.<idx>.top_article.title}}.

examples.prompt: what's the outlook for the IT sector right now?
examples.note: Sector outlook = think AND ground. Start with screen_fundamentals(sector=it) (ranks by ROE), then compare_performance on the top names; optionally get_symbol_news. Never answer with 0 tools / evergreen prose.

examples.prompt: why is nifty down today?
examples.note: State the actual level + change% from get_index_level, THEN chain get_top_movers (losers) to name real movers (and get_symbol_news on the biggest). Do not omit the number; do not defer with "if you want I can check losers".
